text: Since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same resolve, because whoever has suffered in the flesh is done with sin,
so as to live the rest of your time in the flesh no longer by human desires but by the will of God.
For you have spent enough time in the past doing what the Gentiles like to do, living in debauchery, evil desires, drunkenness, wild parties, drinking bouts, and lawless idolatry.

versions.text: You have spent enough time in the past doing what the Gentiles like to do, living in debauchery, lust, drunkenness, wild parties, drinking bouts, and lawless idolatry.
versions.explanation: The connective γάρ links this verse to the previous statement about living for God's will; leaving it untranslated breaks the logical flow of the argument.

versions.text: For you have spent enough time in the past doing what the Gentiles like to do, living in debauchery, lust, drunkenness, wild parties, drinking bouts, and lawless idolatry.
versions.explanation: The list in Greek is a series of plurals (ἀσελγείαις, ἐπιθυμίαις...), and ἐπιθυμίαις echoes ἀνθρώπων ἐπιθυμίαις in verse 2. Rendering it as "evil desires" preserves that verbal link and matches the plural, cumulative force of the list; "lust" narrows the sense to sexual desire alone.

text: They are surprised that you no longer plunge with them into the same flood of reckless living, and so they slander you.
But they will have to give an account to him who stands ready to judge the living and the dead.
This is why the gospel was preached even to the dead: so that, though judged in the flesh as all people are, they might live in the spirit as God lives.

versions.text: This is why the gospel was preached even to the dead: so that, though judged in the flesh as everyone is, they might live in the spirit as God does.
versions.explanation: "as God does" can be misheard as a claim about God's own judging or living identically to believers; "as God lives" with "as all people are" makes the contrast between the human and divine spheres clearer for oral reading.

text: The end of all things is near. So be clear-minded and sober for the sake of your prayers.
Above all, love one another deeply, for love covers over a multitude of sins.

versions.text: Above all, keep your love for one another constant, for love covers a multitude of sins.
versions.explanation: ἐκτενής conveys stretched-out, earnest intensity rather than mere constancy; a simple imperative also reads more naturally aloud.

text: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.
As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another as good stewards of God's varied grace.

Whoever speaks should speak as one delivering the words of God; whoever serves should serve with the strength God supplies, so that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
Dear friends, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal that has come upon you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
Instead, rejoice insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may also rejoice and be overjoyed when his glory is revealed.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you.
None of you, however, should suffer as a murderer or thief or criminal or as a meddler in other people's affairs.
But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed; glorify God that you bear that name.
For it is time for judgment to begin with the household of God; and if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who refuse to obey the gospel of God?

versions.text: For it is time for judgment to begin with the household of God; and if it begins with us, what will be the end of those who refuse to obey the gospel of God?
versions.explanation: πρῶτον ("first") is part of the argument from lesser to greater and should be represented in the translation.

text: And if it is hard even for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?

versions.text: And if the righteous is scarcely saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?
versions.explanation: "the righteous is scarcely saved" is grammatically awkward (a singular adjective used as a noun without a noun) and stumbles when read aloud.

text: So then, those who suffer according to God's will should entrust their souls to a faithful Creator while continuing to do good.
